notice: Presentation taxonomy over existing culture IDs. These are broad catalog classifications, not rigid ethnic, linguistic, territorial or architectural assignments. Source faction and culture data remain unchanged.

aquitani.note: The source uses the broad gallic code. Later testimony distinguishes Aquitani from the Celts/Gauls; do not turn that regional code into a confirmed Celtic identity for 278 BCE.

yuezhi.note: The source uses the broad scythian/Steppe code. This does not establish a Scythian cultural identity. Retained for review without assigning a replacement ethnicity or language.

ligurian-polities.note: The source uses the regional italic code. Do not equate all peoples of ancient Italy with the Italic linguistic family; a more precise grouping requires review.

veneti-italy.note: The source's regional italic code is retained as metadata. A more precise cultural classification is not established by this faction record, so the browser holds it for review rather than inferring ethnic homogeneity.

messapians.note: The source uses the regional italic code. Messapic is distinguished from Italic in the linguistic reference; a precise cultural presentation needs review.
